Tuition teacher's note, end of term
I have taught Kamal and Manoj together for two years. This term Manoj's school test scores rose sharply, into the top five of his class, while his work here stayed the same. Kamal's stayed steady.
Each time results came out, I noticed Kamal went quiet, staring at his notebook, while Manoj celebrated. After the final test Kamal stayed back. He said he had seen Manoj using a cheat sheet in every school test since August. “I told myself it wasn't my business,” he said. “But every time the marks come, I feel sick. Two people who actually studied got pushed below him.”
I told him that feeling uneasy was a signal worth listening to, and that it is not too late to talk to Manoj or a teacher. He has agreed to speak to his class teacher on Monday. I will ask him how it went.

qa.q: Since when had Kamal seen Manoj using a cheat sheet?
qa.a: In every school test since August.

qa.q: How did Kamal feel each time the marks came out?
qa.a: Kamal felt uneasy and sick, knowing honest classmates were being pushed below Manoj.

qa.q: What would have been a better choice back in August?
qa.a: Talking to Manoj privately after the first test, and to a teacher if it continued, before months of unfair marks built up.

qa.q: How are the honest classmates affected by the silence?
qa.a: Two of them who actually studied were pushed below Manoj in rank, losing places they had earned.

grounding: A tuition teacher notes a student who stayed silent about a friend's cheating, watched him gain marks over honest classmates, and felt uneasy at every result.

The results list went up on the notice board today. Chaitanya is third in class. I'm eleventh. I know exactly how he got third.
I've watched him copy from the formula sheet in his calculator cover since the first unit test. I never said anything. I kept telling myself: it's not my business, he's my friend, someone else will notice. Nobody did.
Priyanka studied harder than anyone, and she's fourth. She was crying in the corridor today. She missed third by one mark.
I feel sick about it. Not jealous exactly. More like I'm part of it, because I knew.
Every time I see his name up there, the uneasy feeling comes back. Staying quiet was supposed to be the easy option. It isn't.
Maybe I should talk to him. Or to Ma'am. I don't know yet.
– Zubin
